title: Strain- and Electric-Field-Tunable Valley Polarization in Mo0.75V0.25Te2(Mo3VTe8) for Valleytronic Application
authors: Md. Mostaqul Islam, Vivek Chowdhury, Md. Nure-Alam-Dipu, Ahmed Zubair
abstract: Valley polarization in 2D TMDs is promising for low-power valleytronic and spin-valley information processing, but time-reversal symmetry in pristine nonmagnetic TMDs keeps the K+ and K- valleys degenerate, limiting device applications. In this work, we investigated the structural stability, electronic properties, and tunable valley polarization of V-alloyed MoTe2 monolayer, Mo0.75V0.25Te2, using first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Substitutional alloying of MoTe2 with V introduced magnetic exchange interaction, which, together with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), lifted the valley degeneracy at the unequal valleys. The alloyed structure was found to be energetically and dynamically stable due to the absence of imaginary phonon modes. In pristine MoTe2, SOC produced spin splittings of 34.0 meV and 218.9 meV in the conduction bands and valence bands, respectively, but no valley polarization was observed. In contrast, Mo0.75V0.25Te2 exhibited spontaneous valley polarization of 37.3 meV in the conduction band and 78.2 meV in the valence band. The valley polarization was further enhanced by external electric fields and biaxial strain. A transverse electric field along the crystal c axis produced the maximum valley splitting of 132.8 meV in the valence band, whereas biaxial tensile strain increased the valence band valley splitting up to 160.8 meV. The maximum conduction band valley splitting reached 54.4 meV under 2% biaxial compressive strain. These results demonstrated that V alloying, combined with electric-field and strain engineering, provides an effective strategy for achieving large and tunable valley polarization in MoTe2. Thus, Mo0.75V0.25Te2 can be considered a promising 2D platform for tunable valleytronic device applications, such as transistors and sensors.
summary: This theoretical study investigates $	ext{Mo}_{0.75}	ext{V}_{0.25}	ext{Te}_2$ as a promising 2D platform for valleytronics by using DFT calculations. The authors show that alloying breaks the symmetry of pristine $	ext{MoTe}_2$, inducing valley polarization, which can then be significantly enhanced and tuned using external biaxial strain or electric fields. This work establishes a robust method for engineering materials with controllable valley degrees of freedom.
main_problem: The primary goal is to overcome the valley degeneracy inherent in pristine TMDs, which limits their use in valleytronic devices, by engineering materials that exhibit large and tunable valley polarization.
main_result: V-alloying $	ext{MoTe}_2$ to form $	ext{Mo}_{0.75}	ext{V}_{0.25}	ext{Te}_2$, combined with external electric fields or biaxial strain, successfully induces and enhances valley polarization up to $160.8 	ext{ meV}$.
method: The study relies entirely on first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, including non-collinear treatments for Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), phonon dispersion analysis, and modeling the effects of strain and electric fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Mo}_{0.75}	ext{V}_{0.25}	ext{Te}_2$ monolayer, a transition metal dichalcogenide alloy derived from $	ext{MoTe}_2$. The theoretical framework models electronic structure changes due to alloying (introducing magnetic exchange interaction) and external perturbations like strain ($\epsilon$) and electric fields ($\mathbf{E}$).
key_observables: Valley polarization ($\Delta E = |E_{K^+} - E_{K^-}|$), spin splitting, formation energy ($E_{	ext{formation}}$), phonon frequencies.
important_parameters: Strain levels (e.g., $4\%$ tensile strain), electric field strengths (e.g., $0.4 	ext{ V}/\AA$), and alloying concentrations ($	ext{Mo}_{0.75}	ext{V}_{0.25}	ext{Te}_2$).
main_assumptions: The calculations assume the validity of DFT approximations, including PBE functional and PAW pseudopotentials, to model complex electronic interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures under varying strain/fields, showing polarization enhancement; phonon dispersion confirms dynamic stability for both pristine $	ext{MoTe}_2$ and the alloy; schematic diagrams propose device concepts utilizing this tunability.
paper_structure: The paper systematically progresses from establishing the limitations of pristine TMDs to demonstrating the structural and electronic stability of the V-alloyed material, followed by quantitative analysis of how alloying breaks symmetry, and finally detailing the enhancement mechanisms using external fields and strain for practical device realization.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information protocols, the concept of controlling valley pseudospin via external fields or mechanical strain is a key area in topological/spintronics materials research that interfaces with quantum control concepts.
